plain: Full and complete, with nothing held back

webster.text: Full; entire; complete; as a plenary license; plenary consent; plenary indulgence.

example.quote: They will have authority to farm the revenues and to vest the farmer general, with his subalterns, with plenary powers to collect them, in any way which to them may appear eligible.
example.cite: Brutus VI, New York Journal, Dec. 27, 1787
